title: DiGA@Ortho: Digital health applications in orthopaedics and trauma surgery from the patients' perspective - a mixed-methods study focussing on acceptance, potentials and challenges
summary: Digital health applications, or DiGAs for short, are ‘apps on prescription’ that doctors and psychotherapists have been allowed to prescribe since 2019. In order to investigate the use of DiGAs for knee joint disorders, the patients' perspective on DiGA use is examined with the help of questionnaires at three points in time, telephone interviews and a concluding discussion with various specialist groups.
conditions: Derangement of meniscus due to old tear or injury
Other spontaneous rupture of one or more ligaments of the knee joint: Anterior cruciate ligament
Sprain and strain of the knee joint: rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament
Pain in the extremities: Lower leg [fibula, tibia, knee joint]

interventions.name: The study includes adult patients undergoing orthopaedic care at the university clinics of the Brandenburg Medical School Theodor Fontane with a knee joint disease who are eligible for DiGA use according to the ICD10 diagnostic criteria of the BfArM list. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Prescription of a DiGA, undergoing orthopaedic treatment, German-speaking, a signed declaration of consent is required for all participants to take part in the qualitative study, no signed declaration of consent is required to take part in the questionnaire survey. Participants consent to the survey by ticking the box at the beginning of the questionnaire.
Exclusion criteria:
No DiGA prescription, not undergoing orthopaedic treatment, underage, unable to communicate in German, discontinuation criteria in accordance with the DiGA discontinuation criteria: in the event of a deterioration in general condition such as fever, cold, flu-like infection, dizziness, drowsiness, any acute inflammation, a general feeling of illness or severe pain
